answer_1.quote: We examine self-bias scores on six diverse LLMs, covering four languages across three distinct tasks: machine translation, constrained text generation, and mathematical reasoning.
answer_1.outputs: Generated translations, concept-to-text sentences, and step‑by‑step math solutions

answer_2.quote: We utilized the reference‑based learned metric BLEURT as an approximation of human judgments... To evaluate the coverage of the generated texts, we adopted the evaluation metric used in ... (strict string matching)... We also employ UniEval to measure fluency and understandability.

answer_3.quote: The quality of the text is assessed through self‑feedback from the language model itself... At each feedback step, the LLM generates feedback f_i based on the candidate output y_i... We also replace the self‑evaluation with self‑consistency verification.

answer_4.quote: We employ one graduate student to annotate 50 examples from the 0th and 10th iteration... The human rater compares candidate text against reference and labels error location, error type, and severity labels at candidate text.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators compare each candidate output to the reference translation and label error location, error type, and severity according to MQM style.
